articleTitle: Comparison of Machine Learning Model for Lung Cancer Detection Using Classification Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Lung cancer is one of the most common types of cancer that causes death in the world. In 2020, lung cancer had caused 1,796,144 deaths. This research provides a solution for lung cancer detection using machine-learning classification methods. This research aims to determine the performance of classification algorithms used for building classification models for lung cancer detection. Those algorithms include Support Vector Machine, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Naïve Bayes. The Support Vector Machine algorithm provides performance with an accuracy score of 96.5%, a precision score of 95.83%, and a recall score of 96.66%. The Decision Tree algorithm came up with a performance with an accuracy score of 92%, a precision score of 92.18%, and a recall score of 94.9%. The Random Forest algorithm performs with an accuracy score of 95.5%, a precision score of 95.62%, and a recall score of 94.9%. Moreover, the Naïve Bayes algorithm provides performance with an accuracy score of 80%, a precision score of 79.69%, and a recall score of 80.17%. The comparison of the performance of those four algorithms shows that the Support Vector Machine algorithm provides the best performance in building classification models for lung cancer detection.

articleTitle: Vulnerability Testing and Analysis Using OWASP Top 10 on Academic Information System at University XYZ
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: In the evolving landscape of digital education, Academic Information Systems (AIS) have become essential for managing educational processes and facilitating dynamic learning environments. However, the integration of these systems introduces significant cybersecurity risks that threaten the integrity, availability, and confidentiality of sensitive educational data. This paper presents a vulnerability assessment of the AIS website at University XYZ, conducted using the Open Web Application Security Project (OWASP) guidelines. The methodology includes automated and manual testing with OWASP Zed Attack Proxy (ZAP) to uncover security weaknesses. The penetration testing revealed several vulnerabilities, categorized as medium and low alerts. Medium alerts included the absence of Content Security Policy (CSP) headers, cross-domain misconfigurations, hidden files, missing anti-clickjacking headers, and vulnerable JavaScript libraries. Low alerts included application error disclosures, cookies without secure flags or Same Site attributes, debug error messages, missing Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) headers, and X-Content-Type-Options headers. Based on these findings, practical recommendations such as implementing CSP headers, enabling secure cookie flags and Same Site attributes, configuring HSTS, and adding anti-clickjacking headers were proposed to address these vulnerabilities. By adopting these measures, University XYZ can enhance the security of its AIS, protect sensitive educational data, and maintain the trust of its users.

articleTitle: The Flow Sensor Validation in Spirometer for Automatic Syringe Calibration System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Syringe Calibration is a calibration equipment used for adjusting spirometers. It is in the form of a 3L cylindrical syringe that is currently operated manually. This research aims to create an electric spirometer calibration device that can automatically calibrate the spirometer device. The device uses a stepper motor as a driver for the syringe plunger, which moves back and forth nine times. The Atmega328P IC is used as the controller for the entire working system. The device was tested at the Klaten Islamic Hospital, using the data collection method with 20x data collection. The test results data were compared with a 3L spirometer calibration device, and the calibration process took 140 seconds. The test data showed that the measurement data was changing due to suboptimal sensor readings on the spirometer during the data collection process. The smallest minimum error value obtained in the testing process was 0.1%, and the largest error was 1.2 %, which was still within the tolerance limit range of ±10%.

articleTitle: Expert System for Identifying Pests on Ipomea Batatas Using Bayes Theorem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Sweet potato is a globally important food crop. Ipomoea batatas cultivation faces several challenges in various regions. Pest and disease problems are significant obstacles. Ipomoea batatas farmers need a pest identification system to deal with existing problems. To overcome this problem, an expert system using methods such as Bayes' theorem has been developed to help diagnose pests. A pest identification system in sweet potatoes using the Bayes method has been successfully created. The system calculation has been tested, and the results are manual calculations. Then, the system is re-tested by users and experts. In this test, 35 data from users are processed by the system, and the results are compared by expert identification. The percentage of match between the results of the identification system processing and the experts is 80%.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimization of Half Car Suspension and System Identification with Artificial Neural Networks Using Matlab
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The suspension system in a vehicle plays an important role in ensuring user comfort and safety by dampening vibrations from uneven road surfaces, maintaining vehicle stability, and ensuring contact between the wheels and the road. The half-car suspension model is a simple but effective representation for understanding and controlling the vertical and pitch dynamics of a vehicle. This model is includes the sprung and unsprung mass at the front and rear of the vehicle. In this research, a half-car suspension model is employed to analyze these dynamics, focusing on three prominent system identification methods: NLARX, Transfer Function, and Neural Networks. This model improves predictive performance compared to the linear model, based on the test results, this model achieves high model fit results with the estimated data and a very low Final Prediction Error (FPE). The Transfer Function model is used to represent the input-output relationship of the system in the frequency domain, making it useful for systems that are mostly linear. This Transfer function model gets a fairly good fit value. Neural Network model is also used to gain advantages in capturing complex nonlinear behavior. The results obtained on this Neural Network have higher accuracy in predicting system responses, especially in systems that operate outside the linearity range. Based on the tests conducted, the best validation performance achieved is 0.026939 at epoch 3, indicating good alignment between the actual and predicted displacement responses for the front and rear suspensions. This study compares the three methods based on model fit and FPE. Comparative analysis shows that combining these methods improves the predictive performance of the model, resulting in a more accurate and adaptive vehicle suspension system. This approach can improve the overall performance and optimization of the half-car suspension model.

articleTitle: Design of Improved Fractional Filter Based IMC-PID Controller for SOPTD Process Using ISE Minimisation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This article concentrates on the design of PID based on a prominent IMC (Internal Model Control) scheme in combination with fractional filter to achieve control over a SOPTD (Second Order plus Time Delay) system, which is one among the most common type of system found in industrial applications. The structure of the controller consists of IMC based PID and an IMC filter which is fractional in nature. An optimum higher order fractional IMC filter structure is chosen and additionally Pade's procedure is incorporated for higher order approximation of time delay. The performance of the controller is determined by the IMC filter structure used for designing the controller. Here, the control parameter which include controller gains and coefficients of fractional filter are optimized using ISE (Integral Square Error) minimization. Simulations have been carried on a generic second order system with significant time delay with the help of Simulink model and math script developed for control parameter optimization. The performance of the control strategy with proposed control parameter values in tracking the set point is evaluated by comparing the obtained results with the existing conventional control schemes present in the literature, by comparing the standard performance metrics yielded through them. The robustness of the controller is also tested by analyzing its performance under the influence of disturbance and also the efficiency of the controller in tackling the measurement noise is also observed. Also, analysis is carried out on all the mentioned controllers to investigate the performance deterioration for uncertainties in the controller parameter. The proposed control parameters obtained using ISE minimization shows improved closed loop performance in terms of disturbance rejection and set point tracking.

articleTitle: Engineering Innovation in Aerospace Industry: Review of Technology Applications and Challenges for a Sustainable Future
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The impact of technological engineering applications is crucial for the sustainable future of the aerospace industry. Advancements in maintenance activities and human reliability analysis need to be explored. Therefore, the purpose of this study is to examine the aspects that support domains characterizing future technological engineering innovations in aerospace. Relevant literature on technical information and industry development trends is explored to reveal the trends and challenges in implementing technology within the aerospace field. Challenges in the field of Human Reliability Analysis (HRA), HRA reviews, methods, and data sources are presented. This paper anticipates system failures, provides technical insights, and assesses the readiness of human resources in managing the reliability of complex aerospace industry systems. The paper also emphasizes the importance of synergy between frameworks to ensure comprehensive reliability in the aerospace industry.

articleTitle: AI-Driven MPPT: A Paradigm Shift in Solar PV Systems for Achieving maximum Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This paper accounts for study and comparison about AI-based MPPT algorithm for PV systems. These algorithms choose maximum power point for each cycle by analyzing voltage-current characteristics. They employ a dynamic adaptive voltage range for optimal operation and utilize AI based algorithms. Conventional MPPT algorithms struggle to track maximum power points and thereby resulting in low efficiency. A powerful and responsive MPPT system is necessary to account for time-variant and unpredictable irradiance profiles and considering other environmental conditions as well and that's what we will get to know in the comparison and study through this study. The Results of decision tree algorithm found satisfactory in comparison of other algorithms.

articleTitle: Enhancement on the Mechanical Properties of Dissimilar Friction Stir Welded Aluminum Alloys Potential for Aircraft Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This study investigates the effect of feed rate variation on the mechanical properties of dissimilar aluminum alloy joints, specifically Al 2524-T3 and Al 7055-T7, created through Friction Stir Welding (FSW). Using feed rates of 45, 60, and 75 mm/min at a fixed spindle speed of 1500 rpm and a tilt angle of 2°, we evaluated bending strength, Brinell hardness, and a Mechanical Property Index (MPI) to assess weld quality. Results indicate that a feed rate of 75 mm/min yields the highest bending strength (215.15 MPa) and hardness (42.81 BHN), correlating with an MPI of 1.0, which demonstrates optimal performance. The lower feed rates resulted in lower mechanical properties due to insufficient heat generation. This work highlights the critical influence of feed rate on FSW joint quality in aerospace-relevant dissimilar aluminum alloys.

articleTitle: Nova PM Sensor SDS011 for Alternative Air Quality Monitoring Based on the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Poor air quality is becoming a global issue that impacts human health and the environment. Accurate, real-time air quality measurements are essential for monitoring and addressing these challenges. Currently, the air quality monitoring process is still conducted manually, with tools that tend to be expensive and results that are difficult for the public to access. Additionally, a lack of understanding in analyzing air quality data poses a significant challenge for real-time monitoring. This research aims to design an alternative air quality monitoring device that can provide real-time information using the SDSOll sensor and ESP32 module. The SDS011 sensor measures PM2.5 and PM10 particulate matter in the air, while the ESP32 module acts as a data processor that wirelessly transmits measurement results to a server via a Wi-Fi network. The SDS011 sensors are calibrated using air quality standards. The development of this device includes both hardware and software design, as well as integration between the sensor and communication module. The research aims to develop cost-effective, accurate, and efficient air quality monitoring tools to detect PM2.5 and PM10 levels. It was found that air quality data could be transmitted in real time and made accessible to the public via the ThingSpeak website.

articleTitle: 3D Horror Game Development Using Unity: Evaluation of Human Psychology Through Horror Game
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Games are made for entertainment purposes and have become more relevant over time. Thanks to advances in technology, game development has become more efficient thanks to game engines such as Unity. With this technology, the author developed a 3D Horror Game called “Whispers of the Dark”. This horror game is made to evaluate the players’ psychological aspects. The creation of this game follows the Game Development Life Cycle gradually from Ideation to Deployment. Beta testing will be conducted online and will be done to get feedback from testers. This feedback helps the author to improve the shortcomings in the game. Most respondents to the survey gave a positive response to the game that had been developed.

articleTitle: Texture Features-Based Machine Learning for Classification of Cervical Cell Microscopic Images
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Machine learning has been developed in biomedical science as a clinical decision-support technique. It can automatically recognize patterns in a given dataset to perform predictions and data classification. It has been widely applied to detect abnormalities in various diseases by leveraging texture-based features. This study utilized a Histogram of Oriented Gradients (HOG) as a feature extraction method and a Support Vector Machine (SVM) for classification in detecting the level of cancer abnormalities in cervical cells. The dataset of cervical cell microscopic images consisted of 972 images for training and 108 for testing. Among the models used, the Medium Gaussian SVM achieved the best performance, with a training accuracy of 73.3% and the fastest training time of 4.123 seconds. Whereas, the best performance matrix of testing results achieved 81.10% of accuracy. These results highlight the potential of the proposed method in improving cervical cancer detection through automated and efficient classification techniques.

articleTitle: Development of Speaker Verification System Using Three-Dimensional Feature
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: A speaker verification system purpose is to verify person's ID from their voice. Those voices are processed in the feature extraction process to obtain its voices characteristic or feature. Generally, the feature extraction process generates two-dimensional data as the voice's feature. In this paper, the features extraction is tried to output the voice's characteristic as the three-dimension data or as called as spectrogram. Because the speaker verification system needs a threshold value, in this paper, it is calculated using mean similarity score that resulted from the Euclidean distance value and structural similarity (SSIM) score. The Euclidean distance and SSIM are also used as the system classifier. The experiment shows that the verification applying the proposed method and Euclidean distance obtain 85.33% for the Euclidean classifier, and 82.67% for the SSIM classifier.

articleTitle: Augmented Reality for Introduction the Bravo As202 Aircraft's Components
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Many learning media are used in education to provide lessons to students, especially elementary school children. The electrical media usually include 2D and 3D images, music, video, animation, virtual reality, and augmented reality to attract and increase the learning power of elementary school children. This lesson explains the components of the Bravo As202 aircraft based on Augmented Reality with elementary school students. It is hoped that with this learning media, students can know and understand aircraft components. The method used is the Multimedia Development Life Cycle, which has six stages: concept, design, material collecting, assembly, testing, and distribution using AR Marker Augmented Reality. Based on the test results from the research that has been done, this learning media can be used on Android 10 and 11 smartphones to help provide information about aircraft components and is suitable for use. The application runs well on various smartphones, as evidenced by the user device testing data. The application is feasible to use, as evidenced by the results of the questionnaire answers by the user, which had a percentage of 83.3%.

articleTitle: Implementation of U-Net for Aerial Imagery Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The development of environmental mapping and monitoring technology has been advancing rapidly in recent years, thanks to improvements in remote sensing and drone technology. Drones have become a valuable tool for collecting high-resolution aerial imagery data quickly and efficiently. This data has numerous applications, including image segmentation, environmental monitoring, and natural resource management. One of the main challenges in using aerial imagery is object segmentation, which involves separating specific objects from the background of the image. This research focuses on implementing and evaluating the U-Net model for object segmentation of buildings, rice fields, and runways in aerial imagery. Using aerial imagery data from Google Earth, the study explores various technical aspects of the U-Net model, such as data preprocessing, model training, and performance evaluation. The results demonstrate that the U-Net model is capable of accurately and efficiently segmenting buildings, rice fields, and runways. This research has the potential to significantly contribute to the field of aerial imagery segmentation and expand the practical applications of the U-Net model in aerial resource monitoring and management scenarios.

articleTitle: Implementation of Forward Kinematics Methods on Weight-Based Sorting Arm Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The arm robot is a type of manipulator that resembles a human arm. This robot can be used as an automated system for sorting items, including sorting items based on their weight. The process of sorting items based on their weight can utilize the Load Cell sensor as a measuring tool to determine the weight of the items to be sorted. The application of the forward kinematics method to the robot arm is one of the approaches used to control robot movement towards the goal position. Based on this explanation, the researcher aims to implement the forward kinematics method on the robot arm as a sorter of items based on weight. The operation of this tool begins with an object that runs on a conveyor and will automatically fall on the scale. The Load Cell Sensor will send data on the weight of the item to the microcontroller, which then sends it to the arm robot as forward kinematics calculation data. After receiving the data, the arm robot will grab the items and move them to the appropriate place based on their weight specifications. There are four weight categories that will be sorted, namely; 80 grams, 100 grams, 120 grams, and 180 grams.

articleTitle: Towards AI Chatbot Effectiveness: Crucial Elements Impacting User Engagement and Satisfaction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Recently, chatbots have been the most influential applications of artificial intelligence in changing user interactions across various industries. This paper presents the changing landscape of AI chatbot or conversational AI implementation, focusing on challenges and strategic approaches to enhance user engagement and adoption. Next-generation AI chatbots are empowered to understand and respond to user queries more accurately and relevantly through the support of natural language processing and machine learning. However, there are still huge challenges to be overcome regarding user experience optimization, frustration reduction, and trust building. This research has singled out eight factors that influence artificial intelligence chatbot performance in various domains, with the objective of improving this design and functionality. By taking these challenges and leveraging strategic implementation, the organizations can maximize the value of AI chatbots in enhancing customer engagement and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: The Analysis of E-Retribution Readiness and Effectiveness in Regional Levies Compliance Efforts
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: According to Sustainability Development Goals number 11 about sustainable cities and communities, all region must be making their cities and communities strong and resilient region especially in Indonesia. To make a strong cities and communities every region in Indonesia must have some innovation to develop their region especially using technology. This research was conducted to analyze how far E-Retribution's effectiveness in helping people and the market managers do payment to comply with levy payments and ERetribution readiness to increase levy payment compliance. In many cases people in local region aren't complying in paying taxes especially in levy payments because of the difficulty to pay. To know how effective ERetribution can help people increasing regional levies payment compliance so this research come to answer this problem. This Research using Qualitative method and using In Depth Interview in collecting data.

articleTitle: Improvement of PID Based on Fuzzy Logic Controller for Controlling Attitude of a Quadcopter
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The quadcopter has a fairly simple mechanical design because it does not require other drives to perform various movements such as roll, pitch, and yaw. The simplicity of this mechanical design has a considerable impact on the complexity of its control. Therefore, it is necessary to have a good control method to maintain the stability of the quadcopter. The research aims to maintain stability of quadcopter by using a combination of the Fuzzy Logic Controller (FLC) with the Proportional-Integral-Derivative (PID) method, where FLC is used to initialize the input of the PID method to find the quadcopter stability point. The application of fuzzy methods for the initial tuning of PID parameters has proven effective in enhancing the system's fundamental performance, such as overshoot, rise time, and settling time, compared to the conventional PID approach. The proposed method can reduce overshoot by over 20%, with reductions reaching up to 88% in yaw motion. Additionally, the Fuzzy-PID approach significantly improves stability, shortening the time to achieve steady-state by less than 1 seconds for all movements while PID did more than 2s for pitch and roll motions and over 1s for yaw motion.

articleTitle: A Review: Recommendation System for Risk Analysis at Universities Using Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: In this research, the TF-IDF method is used in the application of risk analysis recommendation system at universities based on Natural Language Processing (NLP). Each university has several work units, where each work unit has various activities within a budget year that have several categories of risks associated with the achievement of those activities. Risk analysis for each activity is important in the planning process so that all planned activities can be successfully as the planning. Furthermore, risk management utilizing text classification and this risk analysis will be tested by the Internal Audit Unit as an evaluator of each work unit's activities to determine whether the text classification and risk analysis methods will function effectively. In this research phase, a Data Science-based methodology is adopted, with a primary focus on text data processing through NLP techniques to generate relevant recommendations. The results of this research, through concept validation, can provide recommendations for various activities in higher education based on risk levels. The system developed using the TF -IDF method promises to be applied in higher education institutions that wish to plan activities and prepare for the risk levels of several planned works.

articleTitle: Internet of Things System for Melon/Watermelon Plant Growth with Image-Based Fruit Weight Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This research develops an Internet of Things (IoT) system for watering automation and growth monitoring of melon and watermelon plants, with image processing-based fruit weight prediction. Through sensors of soil moisture, temperature, air humidity, and light intensity, the system automatically regulates watering based on environmental conditions, so that plants get water efficiently and in a timely manner. In addition, the system is equipped with a camera used to take pictures of fruits, which are then analyzed using image processing algorithms to automatically predict fruit weight. This research integrates IoT, image processing, and cloud computing technologies in one connected system, thus providing a comprehensive solution for irrigation management and crop monitoring. It is expected that this system can improve water use efficiency, reduce manual intervention, and provide more accurate crop yield predictions, thus supporting more productive and sustainable smart agriculture. This research evaluates the accuracy of soil sensors and a CNN model in agricultural monitoring, achieving high reliability with nutrient (99.9998%), pH (99.05440/0), and moisture (99.3827%) sensors, as well as fruit weight prediction (99.25% to 99.93%). These results confirm the system's suitability for precision agriculture, with ongoing developments to enhance the application interface.

articleTitle: Aircraft Flight Schedule Announcement at Pionir Indonesian Airport Based on SMS Broadcast
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The design and construction of delivering announcements using a web-based SMS gateway aims to help overcome problems that often occur at pioneer airports; this is because when passengers want to travel, many passengers still arrive late to check-in, even though the passenger ticket has a notification for checking. -in 1 hour before Departure. If a flight's Departure is delayed or accelerated, passengers will only receive this information when they arrive at the airport, whereas if at the time the departure notification is delayed or accelerated, the passenger is still outside the airport or still on their way to the airport, as a result, they will definitely not receive the information. Testing voice announcements on parking, arrival, departure, delay, check-in, and waiting room services, as well as testing SMS broadcasts (30 user numbers and one airline), shows that the announcement application provides information through voice data recording and broadcasts SMS to passengers and families. Testing was carried out at Indonesian Pioner airport for 30 passengers for a week. The percentage of Ease of obtaining test voice information was 81.98%, and the percentage of Ease of obtaining broadcast SMS information was 83.1%. Implementing the announcement is feasible at pioneer airports with a percentage of 82.54%.

articleTitle: Open Computer Based Test (OCBT) Using the Linear Congruent Method at SMA Angkasa Yogyakarta
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This research aims to create open computer-based test (CBT) software so that schools in Indonesia can use it. The method used in this CBT is the randomization of Lienar Congruent Method questions. Testing was carried out at Angkasa yogyakarta High School (SMA) with the results of questions number one to forty of the ten students who used it being different. The application of LCM is to determine the initial parameters that are used as a benchmark for randomization so that it can produce a random number. The parameters used include multiplier factor, addition factor, modulus, and prefix or seed value. The result of this research is the randomization of questions using the Linear Congruent Method (LCM) in the Indonesian language subject, questions number 1 - 40 for each student were randomized and were successful with an accuracy score of 100%.

articleTitle: FPV Camera Technology Provides a Nutrition Service Robot System for Patients Suffering from Infection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The rise of infectious diseases has heightened the demand for technology that reduces direct contact between healthcare professionals and patients. This study seeks to develop a food delivery robot system that employs First-Person View (FPV) camera technology to improve the safety of medical personnel and patients. This device is engineered to remotely deliver sustenance to infected persons in isolation rooms, hence mitigating the risk of viral transmission. The FPV camera enables the operator to oversee and guide the robot's movements in real-time from a distance, assuring accurate navigation and secure delivery. This robot features a control system linked to a wireless network, facilitating operational versatility in a medical setting. The robot features three velocity settings: 0.25 m/s (level 1), 0.34 m/s (level 2), and 0.43 m/s (level 3). Measurement results indicate that the battery capacity enables the robot to operate for 2 hours. The measured average static speeds are 2.367 m/s for level 1, 2.460 m/s for level 2, and 2.668 m/s for level 3 at 1.2 m/s. Research findings demonstrate that food delivery robots outfitted with FPV cameras can diminish the risk of infection transmission and improve operational efficiency in healthcare environments.

articleTitle: Visualization of Malware on Android Applications Using Static Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The abundance of software at software download service providers attracts smartphone users to download and use the available software. Not all available software has good security guarantees when used by smartphone users. This research examines the software on the Google Play store, which provides money lending and gaming services. We scanned 50 pieces of software with Virus Total and ESET Security, which analyzed and visualized our scan data using an application we created in Python. The visualization results show that 40 out of 50 applications have indications of malware in them. As many as 86% of the 40 applications contained adware, and 14% contained trojans. This reminds smartphone owners to be careful when downloading applications to avoid anything detrimental to them.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Causes of Corrosion in the Seat Track Section 43 Area on a Boeing 737-300 Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Corrosion is one of the significant issues affecting the reliability and longevity of aircraft components. This study aims to analyze the causes of corrosion in the seat track area of section 43 on the Boeing 737-300 aircraft. The methods used in this study include investigating the aircraft's operating environment, focusing on factors such as humidity, temperature, and chemical contamination that can accelerate the corrosion process. The results show that the corrosion in the seat track area of section 43 is caused by a combination of factors, including high humidity in the operating environment, the presence of chemical contaminants such as salt and fuel, and the use of materials less resistant to corrosion. The recommended countermeasures include improving maintenance procedures, emphasizing routine cleaning to remove contaminants, using more corrosion-resistant materials, and applying protective coatings to vulnerable areas. Implementing these measures is expected to reduce the incidence of corrosion in the seat track area of section 43 on the Boeing 737-300, thereby enhancing safety and extending the aircraft's service life. Keywords: corrosion, seat track, Boeing 737-300, cargo plane

articleTitle: Simulation of Water Sensing Automatic Windshield Wiper Device with Microcontroller-Based LCD Display
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The simulation of the Water Sensing automatic windshield wiper with an LCD display based on a microcontroller was created using several methods, including design, which involves creating block diagrams, flowcharts, and designing schematic diagrams, and production, which includes component installation (soldering), acrylic assembly, programming the Arduino Nano microcontroller, and packaging the device. The main components of this device are the raindrop sensor, Arduino Nano, 12 × 6 LCD, and servo motor. Simulation of the Water Sensing automatic windshield wiper with an LCD display based on a microcontroller has been successfully created. The functional testing process went well, resulting in the device being able to detect the presence of rainwater, activate the wiper lever (wiper link), and move according to the intensity of the rain. Additionally, the device can also display information regarding the level of rain intensity on the LCD screen. This tool is expected to broaden knowledge and can be studied by students and readers alike, both in terms of its operation and its manufacturing process, so that it can be developed in the future, making this system beneficial, especially for the aviation industry and society in general.

articleTitle: Modelling Self-Balancing Robot using ARX and Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This paper considers how to model a two-wheeled self-balancing robot (TWSB) using ARX algorithm and artificial neural network to improve the efficiency of PID control system. The dynamic model of the robot is developed using state-space representation, and system identification is performed to compare linear models such as ARX and other models including neural networks. The implementation of the neural network algorithm demonstrates improved stability and faster response time, achieving balance in less than 5 seconds. Experimental results show a significant reduction in error, with the Mean Square Error (MSE) reaching as low as 0.082256, highlighting the significant differences between the two-wheeled self-balancing robot and the two-wheeled self-balancing robot.

articleTitle: Usability Evaluation of Railway Component Supply Chain Management Information System Using System Usability Scale
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Supply chain management is an urgent factor for supporting of a company business and production, including on railway component industry. In this study we present a usability measurement of railway component supply chain management information system, called Rekachain using System Usability Score (SUS). Based on the conducted study, it gathered SUS score of Rekachain application is 73,54, which is categorized with grade B-. It indicates that the system is excellent and acceptable. But this application still needs an improvement in two aspects of usability, which are memorability and errors.

articleTitle: Optimizing Credit Card Fraud Detection Using a Hybrid Sampling Approach with SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Credit card fraud detection remains a significant challenge due to the highly imbalanced nature of transactional datasets, where fraudulent transactions represent only a tiny fraction. This paper presents a hybrid sampling approach that integrates Adaptive Synthetic Sampling (ADASYN), Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), and Random Undersampling to address this imbalance, using a Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifier. The proposed method was evaluated using a real-world credit card dataset and compared to traditional resampling techniques. Results demonstrate that the hybrid approach significantly improves the detection of fraudulent transactions. The SVM model trained with SMOTE achieved an Fl-score of 0.9290 and an AUC-ROC score of 0.9306, slightly outperforming the ADASYN-based model. This study highlights the effectiveness of combining different resampling techniques to enhance fraud detection in imbalanced datasets.

articleTitle: Impact of SMOTE and Feature Selection on SVM and KNN Performance in Smoker Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This research classifies the smoker status dataset using two algorithms, i.e., Support Vector Machine (SVM) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). Researchers used several kernels in the SVM model: linear, RBF, and Polynomial. Researchers implemented K values of 3 and 110 in the KNN model. This study uses two data types: the original data of 55692 rows and the data balanced by applying SMOTE of 70474. The evaluation results show that the linear kernel SVM method with the SMOTE process and forward selection method produces the highest accuracy of 76%. In comparison, the accuracy of the KNN method with the SMOTE process and using all features get the highest accuracy of 84%. This research shows that the application of SMOTE can improve model performance. In addition, the application of feature selection also affects the accuracy results except for the KNN model on SMOTE data using all features.

articleTitle: Trees have Ears: An Acoustic Surveillance and TinyML-Based for Detecting Illegal Logging
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This study presents an innovative acoustic surveillance system utilizing TinyML to detect illegal logging in the rainforests of the Philippines. To overcome the limitations of traditional methods, the researchers integrated acoustic data capture with machine learning algorithms on the RP2040 microcontroller. Two feature extraction methods—spectrogram and Mel Filterbank Energy (MFE)—were compared for training machine learning models in both binary and multiclass sound classification tasks. The spectrogram-based binary model demonstrated exceptional accuracy, efficient resource utilization, and fast execution, making it ideal for resourceconstrained environments. Meanwhile, the MFE binary model excelled in real-world acoustic analysis and performed well in multiclass classification, achieving 84.4% accuracy at an 8 kHz sampling rate and 89.6% at 16 kHz. Furthermore, tests confirmed reliable chainsaw sound detection up to 20 meters away. These findings offer an effective solution for illegal logging detection and provide valuable insights into optimizing models based on context and hardware configurations. This system contributes significantly to global efforts in ecosystem monitoring and conservation.

articleTitle: Utilization of Asynchronous Learning as an Innovation in Independent Learning of IoT Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The increasing popularity of integrating C programming learning curricula on the Internet of Things (IoT) using Arduino has become an increasingly common trend in vocational education programs. This curriculum introduces students to Arduino as the main platform used to understand IoT concepts. Students are involved in the learning process by reading module materials and writing program codes, although they often face challenges when errors occur in the code they create. In addition, other obstacles that arise are the time required to synchronize and configure in the Arduino IDE development environment, as well as the difficulty in auditing students' work by teachers. These problems can hinder the smooth learning process, considering that IoT programming involves complex structures and is closely related to the hardware and sensors used in IoT projects. This study focuses on learning C programming for IoT applications developed using Arduino. The aim is to overcome the difficulties faced by students and teachers in the process of learning and teaching IoT programming. As a solution, a self-learning system known as “Asynchronous Learning” has been designed and developed. This system provides students with the ability to learn IoT programming independently, with their work processed through the use of the Test-driven Development (TDD) method. The results of the students' work are then analyzed using the T-Test and can be accessed through a web platform provided.

articleTitle: The Effect of Switching Capacitor Banks on Transient Phenomena in Electric Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This study evaluates the impact of switching capacitor banks on transient phenomena in power systems. Capacitor banks are often used to improve efficiency through power factor improvement and voltage stabilization, but switching can cause significant current and voltage spikes, called transient phenomena. These phenomena can disrupt electrical devices, degrade power quality, and damage sensitive components. This study analyzes the effects of several capacitor bank configurations, including a capacitor bank with a reactor and a capacitor bank with a solid-state (IGBT), on transient parameters such as current, voltage, duration, and transient frequency. The research methodology combines experimental and simulation approaches, with schematic diagrams illustrating the relationship between capacitor bank switching and transient characteristics concerning system parameters, such as current, voltage, active power, and reactive power. The results show that the standard capacitor bank produces a voltage spike of 289.87 V, a peak current of 43.83 A, a transient duration of 1.66 ms, and a frequency of 602.40 Hz. The addition of a reactor reduces the transient frequency to 100 Hz and the peak current to 8.48 A, but extends the transient duration to 10 ms. In contrast, solid-state (IGBT) shortens the transient duration to 1.25 ms at a frequency of 800 Hz. This study recommends configurations to minimize the negative impact of transients, thereby improving power system stability.

articleTitle: aBLE: A Bluetooth Low Energy Hotel Asset Tracker
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This study presents a Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) Hotel Asset Tracker designed to transform asset management in hotel environments. Despite the underutilization of asset tracking solutions in the hospitality industry, this research develops a tailored, efficient system using BLE technology and beacon transmitters. The system provides real-time tracking of essential hotel room assets, such as luggage racks, blankets, remotes, and other amenities. Evaluation results show an impressive 98% accuracy rate in room identification and high user satisfaction. The mean SEQ rating, based on feedback from 23 participants, is approximately 6.26 out of 7, indicating that users found the system very easy to use, with most rating their experience as “Very Easy” or “Easy.” While feedback highlights the need for improvements, such as clearer instructions and smaller tag sizes, the system demonstrates its potential to improve operational efficiency and guest satisfaction. This research marks a significant advance in utilizing technology to address persistent challenges in the hospitality sector.

articleTitle: Adisutjipto Institute of Aerospace Technology Virtual Tour with Artificial Intelligence (AI) Agent
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This study aims to develop an interactive virtual tour based on Android with a first-person shooter approach to introduce the Adisutjipto Institute of Aerospace Technology (ITD Adisutjipto) virtually. This virtual tour utilizes an Artificial Intelligence (AI) agent as an intelligent guide who can answer questions and provide relevant information related to facilities and locations inside the ITD Adisutjipto building. The test results show that this virtual tour is effective and feasible to use, with a user satisfaction rate reaching 87.72%. This study contributes to the field of educational virtual technology by offering a more immersive and interactive experience. Users can easily explore the ITD Adisutjipto building virtually and obtain the information they need efficiently. This research is expected to be an innovative solution to introduce the ITD Adisutjipto to wider community, as well as support learning and research activities in the aerospace technology field.

articleTitle: Building Custom Large Language Models for Industries: A Comparative Analysis of Fine-Tuning and Retrieval-Augmented Generation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: In this study, we delve into the development and optimization of custom Large Language Models (LLMs) tailored for specific industrial applications, concentrating on two predominant adaptation techniques: fine-tuning and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). We employ a rigorous, mathematically-driven approach to compare the efficacy of these methodologies, using a dual dataset derived from TACIT Company, which specializes in the tacit knowledge of retiring workforce documentation, and Sight Machine, which focuses on manufacturing process data. Our evaluation framework uses three metrics: Accuracy, calculated as the ratio of correctly predicted instances to total predictions; Adaptability, which measures the model's performance stability when exposed to novel, evolving datasets; and Industry Relevance, assessed through expert-based qualitative scoring converted to quantitative analysis. This comprehensive comparative analysis not only quantifies the performance differences between finetuning and RAG but also explores the computational dynamics and potential synergies when implementing these models. Additionally, we address the ethical considerations and practical implications of deploying LLMs in sensitive industries, framing these technologies within the context of operational integrity and data governance. The outcome of this research aims to guide stakeholders in selecting and optimizing LLM strategies that align with specific industrial needs, balancing technical efficiency, and ethical standards.

articleTitle: SCM and CPM Enhancement with AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Technology has transformed the supply chain industry by improving transaction authentication, transparency, efficiency, and trust. This study explores advancements in supply chain management, focusing on traceability, smart contracts, inventory management, and regulatory compliance in sectors like food, agriculture, healthcare, retail, and automotive. Emphasis is placed on mitigating the bullwhip effect and integrating tools such as the PERT network to reduce delays and critical path times. Despite challenges such as scalability, regulatory compliance, and industry acceptance, AI has the potential to revolutionize supply chain processes, enhancing decentralization, transparency, and tracking from source to delivery. Widespread adoption is hindered by the expertise needed for implementation and varying government regulations. Over time, transparency-based technology is likely to replace traditional processes.

articleTitle: Enhancing PCB Quality Control with Deep Learning Based Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Ensuring high-quality PCBs is crucial for reliable electronic devices. Traditional inspection methods are often time-consuming and prone to errors, leading to the need for more efficient and accurate defect detection techniques. This research explores the use of deep learning models to enhance PCB quality control by automating the detection of defects such as missing holes, mouse bites, short circuits, and spurious copper. The research employed three object detection models: YOLOv8n, Faster R-CNN R50 FPN, and RetinaNet R50 FPN to detect and classify PCB defects. Data augmentation techniques such as horizontal/vertical flipping, grayscale conversion, hue adjustment, noise addition, saturation, blur, and brightness adjustments were applied to further improve model performance. Through comprehensive training on a labeled PCB dataset, the models were evaluated based on metrics such as mAP (mean Average Precision) and total loss. The results showed that YOLOv8n achieved the highest accuracy with a mAP@50 of 89.3% and mAP@50-95 of 45%, along with a superior inference speed of 5.9ms. Faster R-CNN R50 FPN followed with a mAP@50 of 85.9% and mAP@50-95 of 41.9%, and RetinaNet R50 FPN achieved a mAP@50 of 71.6% and mAP@50-95 of 34.5%. The results underscore YOLOv8n's suitability for real-time defect detection due to its combination of high accuracy and fast processing speed, while the other models, although improved after augmentation enhancement, did not match its performance. This research demonstrates the potential of deep learning models for automating PCB defect detection with high accuracy and efficiency, focusing on ordinary single-layered PCB surfaces. While effective, it does not address defect detection in multi-layered PCBs and faces challenges like defect complexity, data imbalance, and limited samples. Future work can explore multi-layered PCBs, improve model robustness and generalization, employ advanced augmentation techniques, and enhance model interpretability for practical reliability.

articleTitle: A Combined Approach to Safety and Security of IoT Based on Fault Attack Tree
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Safety and security are critical considerations when it comes to the Internet of Things (IoT), as the interconnected nature of IoT devices introduces new risks and vulnerabilities. To address these challenges, a combined approach that integrates Fault Tree Analysis (FTA) and Attack Trees (AT) can be employed to enhance the safety and security of IoT systems. FTA focuses on identifying faults and failures that can lead to safety hazards, while AT focuses on identifying attack vectors and potential security breaches. Combining FTA and AT, we can identify the potential causes of failures in a system and how an attacker can exploit those failures. This information can then be used to design countermeasures to prevent accidental failures and intentional attacks. This approach leverages both proactive and reactive techniques to ensure the robustness of IoT systems. By integrating the two approaches, organizations can develop a more robust and resilient IoT system that addresses both safety and security concerns.

articleTitle: Gamifying Big Data Education: an RPG Approach with Integrated Quiz Assessments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The increasing need for Big Data education makes it harder to keep students interested and make sure they remember difficult ideas. By creating the educational role-playing game “Data Quest: Big Data Adventure,” which incorporates quiz evaluations based on the Achievement-Based Unlocking System, this study tackles these problems. The goal of the study is to use an interactive learning platform to increase students' motivation and comprehension of big data. The study involved students from SMKN 10 Malang focus on 30 students selected specifically for pre-and post-tests to measure learning outcomes and motivation. Data was gathered through surveys, questionnaires, and pre- and post-tests. According to the statistical analysis, post-test scores significantly improved, gain score 0.54 overall across the five Big Data concepts (Volume, Variety, Velocity, Veracity, and Value). In terms of student interest, the results showed high levels of engagement with overall average score 81.19%, demonstrating the effectiveness of gamification as an engagement method. According to qualitative feedback, the game strengthened students' comprehension of difficult concepts while also being entertaining and instructive. According to the findings, incorporating quiz assessments into educational games through role-playing games offers a viable way to address student disengagement and enhance education learning outcomes.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Optimization of MTPA in IPMSM Drives for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This research presented in this paper outlines a pioneering optimization framework concentrated on perfecting the Maximum Torque per Ampere (MTPA) control mechanism in Interior Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (IPMSM) drives for the realm of electric vehicles (EVs). Through the integration of supervised learning methodologies for parameter forecasting alongside reinforcement learning (RL) techniques for real-time adaptive regulation, the proposed methodology dynamically enhances torque output and energy efficiency across fluctuating driving conditions. The framework employs a Deep Q-Network (DQN) agent to perpetually recalibrate the direct-axis and quadrature-axis currents, establishing an equilibrium between torque production and energy expenditure in a real-time context. The simulation data reveals a potential rise of up to 15% in torque efficiency, a 10% lessening in energy expended, and a 15% prolongation in battery life when juxtaposed with traditional fixed-parameter approaches. This technique surpasses traditional motor control methodologies by prioritizing real-time adaptability and resilience, thus presenting itself as a viable solution for the forthcoming generation of EVs. Subsequent research will investigate the practical application of the proposed framework in real-world scenarios and its adaptability to more intricate operating conditions.

articleTitle: Arduino-Based Automated System for Ammonia Neutralization in Poultry Waste Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: This research addressed the problem of ammonia pollution resulting from chicken farm waste, which posed significant health risks to both livestock and nearby communities. The primary purpose of the study was to develop a smart system prototype designed to manage chicken manure more effectively by eliminating ammonia odor and improving manure production. The method involved designing and developing an automated chemical spraying system based on Arduino, incorporating key components such as LDR sensors, AC and DC motors, solenoid valves, and conveyor belts. The findings revealed that the developed system successfully detected chicken manure automatically and applied the chemicals evenly, proving to be more effective than traditional manual methods. The results indicated a significant reduction in ammonia odor and an enhancement in manure quality. The implications of this research suggest that the introduction of automated technology in farm waste management can improve environmental quality and the health of communities surrounding chicken farms. Additionally, the use of this technology has the potential to increase farm productivity through better waste management and the production of higher-quality manure.

articleTitle: Smart Management of Power Transformers: A GIS and IoT Approach for Improved Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The integration of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) and the Internet of Things (IoT) is explored for smart management of power transformers, essential for maintaining efficient and stable electricity distribution. As the demand for reliable energy grows, advanced technologies are increasingly applied to enhance transformer monitoring and reduce operational downtime. IoT-based sensors enable the system to collect real-time data on transformer conditions, while GIS mapping allows for the visualization of asset locations and performance. This approach supports continuous monitoring, early detection of potential issues, and timely maintenance interventions. By optimizing maintenance scheduling and resource allocation, the system reduces the risk of transformer failures, improves service reliability, and generates significant cost savings. Case studies and simulations demonstrate the effectiveness of this integrated method, highlighting its scalability and potential for widespread implementation in modern power grids. The combination of GIS and IoT offers a data-driven solution to power transformer management, fostering smarter and more resilient electrical infrastructure. Lastly, key findings indicate the system's ability to reduce transformer downtime by up to 30<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, improve maintenance efficiency by 25<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>, and achieve cost savings of approximately 20% compared to conventional methods, showcasing its transformative potential for modern energy management.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of YOLO Models for Safety Helmet Detection: Insights from YOLOv5 to YOLOv10 with Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Head injuries pose a significant risk in industries such as construction and manufacturing, making helmet use essential for safety. This paper presents a comparative analysis of six YOLO (You Only Look Once) models-YOLOv5mu, YOLOv6m, YOLOv7, YOLOv8m, YOLOv9 (m, GELAN-c, GELAN-e), and YOLOv10m-for helmet detection using a public dataset. The models are evaluated for mean Average Precision (mAP), frames per second (FPS), training time, and model size. YOLOv9 (GELAN-e) achieves the highest accuracy with 96.17% mAP at 0.1% confidence and 82.71% at 70% confidence. YOLOv8m is the fastest, achieving 45.37 FPS, while YOLOv10m has the highest mAP (85.10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) at 70% confidence and is the most compact (33.5 MB). YOLOv9 (GELAN-c) offers the shortest training time (1.32 hours), while YOLOv9 strikes the best balance between accuracy, speed, and size. These findings suggest YOLOv9 as an excellent choice for applications requiring both accuracy and efficiency, while YOLOv8m is optimal for real-time scenarios.

articleTitle: Introducing Tourism Spot in Indonesia Using Adventure Video Game
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Video games have been quickly rising to become one of the most popular entertainment media. The relation between a video game and a location can promote or introduce the location to the game's players. On the other hand, Indonesia is a country that has benefited from the tourism industry. The objective of the research itself is to find out if an adventure game can introduce a tourism place in Indonesia effectively and identify features needed for the game for it to be successful in introducing a tourism place. A user requirement survey was conducted and there was a warm reception for using adventure games to introduce a tourism place and according to the respondents, graphics and visuals was the most important aspect of the game. A video game was developed using the Game Development Life Cycle method and the Unity game engine to introduce one tourism place in Indonesia, Tebing Keraton. Using a survey to gather feedback from players, this research found that the game that was developed even though it is generally successful in introducing the tourism place, according to the feedback there are also many things that could be further improved like accessibility of the game, change the game to be an open world setting and adding the introduction of culture as well using non-playable characters or game objects and decorations.

articleTitle: Improving Orientation Estimation Accuracy Using Dynamic Data Fusion of Multiple Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The determination of UAV orientation is a challenging task. This is usually performed by a data fusion from accelerometers, gyroscopes, and magnetometers using a Kalman filter. However, the data fusion of these three-sensor does not always provide accurate orientation data due to various UAV conditions, such as static and dynamic states. Therefore, it is necessary to develop a dynamic data fusion approach that takes these conditions into account. UAV state determination is also an area of ongoing development. Numerous studies have been carried out to precisely assess the sensor's condition. However, the approach involves a relatively intricate algorithm, posing challenges for implementation on microprocessor-based systems. In this study, the determination of dynamic or static conditions is performed by measuring the variance of acceleration data and the total linear acceleration data. The use of this dynamic data fusion method can improve the accuracy of orientation estimation, especially for roll and pitch angles.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Piano Practice: A Game-Based Learning Rhythm Game to Motivate and Support Learners
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Learning piano is a popular activity and hobby for individuals worldwide. However, many learners experience hurdles that cause them to discontinue their studies, such as a decline in motivation and feeling directionless when practicing. To assist piano learners in practicing and regaining their motivation, this study aims to develop a rhythm game for Android devices that uses a physical MIDI keyboard based on the game-based learning concept to increase learner's piano abilities through entertaining and engaging way. The contribution of this research lies in testing the feasibility of using a rhythm game with a physical MIDI keyboard to support piano learners' practice. The GDLC method was implemented for the development process. Based on usability testing, which has the success rate of 100%, this study concludes with the successful development of the game, with challenging game modes, levels, and other game elements, and has successfully enhanced players’ motivation for practicing piano.

articleTitle: Human Following Robot Based on Object Detection for Aerospace Application
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: In this research, the Human Following Robot (HFR) prototype has been designed and implemented using YOLO v3-Tiny and Tensor Flow Lite on Raspberry Pi hardware named Rewang. The HFR Rewang is designed to assist aircraft technicians by bringing maintenance tool kits to aircraft shelters. Rewang's movement is based on a camera as a vision sensor following the movement of human entities. Image input is processed by YOLO v3-Tiny through the determination of the bounding box, the calculation of Euclidean Distance, and the determination of the pixel value of the camera as the basis of Rewang's movement which is regulated by an L298N driver motor that controls two Direct Current (DC) motors for the left and right wheels. The test results show that Rewang can move at an average speed of 0.18 m/s at 2 m with a travel time of 11 seconds with a light intensity of more than 250 lux. The minimum and maximum distance of object detection is as far as 120 cm and 400 cm, with an object detection accuracy of 95.8%. Rewang allows the HFR to have a larger carrying capacity to bring more complete aircraft maintenance tools and is prospective for other aerospace and general applications.

articleTitle: Implementation of Solar Power Plants (PLTS) for Pump System Operation in Environmentally Friendly Vertical Gardens Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: The increasing need for green space in urban areas is a major concern in supporting environmental sustainability. One of the solutions implemented is a vertical garden, a vertical garden that not only beautifies buildings but also helps absorb air pollutants. However, to maintain the survival of plants in vertical gardens, an efficient and environmentally friendly irrigation system is needed. This study aims to develop and implement Solar Power Plants (PLTS) as the main energy source in operating a water pump system in vertical gardens based on the Internet of Things (IoT). This system is designed to utilize solar energy as a renewable energy source, which drives automatic pumps according to plant needs monitored through soil moisture, and temperature. Data from these sensors is sent in real-time to the IoT platform, allowing automatic irrigation settings based on environmental conditions. The IoT-based system also enables effective remote monitoring and control, increasing the efficiency of water use and maintaining the stability of the vertical garden ecosystem. Thus, this research makes a significant contribution to the development of sustainable and environmentally friendly vertical garden technology, especially in the urban context.

articleTitle: Smart Mobile Solution for Sugarcane Disease Identification and Educational Support Using Forward Chaining
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: Sugarcane is a key crop for sugar and biofuel production, supporting tropical economies, but is highly susceptible to diseases and pests that hinder its cultivation. This research focuses on developing an intelligent mobile application for early disease identification and educational support to empower farmers in improving productivity and economic stability. The study follows a structured four-phase framework: Preprocess Design (literature review and stakeholder interviews), Process Design (current condition analysis), Development (data architecture and UI design), and Post Design (implementation and testing). The resulting mobile app enhances farmers' understanding of plant diseases and management strategies using a forward chaining system that combines symptom facts and disease rules for accurate diagnosis. User satisfaction analysis indicates high scores for Responsiveness, Usability, and Error Handling, each exceeding 4.5, while lower ratings in Search (3.76) and Onboarding highlight areas for improvement. This research underscores the potential of smart mobile applications to support sugarcane farmers in disease management and knowledge enhancement, contributing to more effective cultivation practices and improved economic outcomes. By addressing the identified weaknesses in Search and Onboarding, the application has the potential to increase user engagement further and foster long-term loyalty among farmers.

articleTitle: E-Voting Application Development Utilizing Blockchain Technology: Evaluation of Blockchain's Usage to Solve E-Voting Data Security Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: E-Voting is an important role in voting decisionmaking. However, E-Voting has many weaknesses such as lack of data transparency and security in the application, which can reduce public trust. Therefore, the author intends to apply blockchain technology as a method that can solve this problem. The author proposes a solution by utilizing blockchain technology on the Ethereum network and utilizing smart contract technology. By implementing blockchain technology, every voice transaction will be recorded in a decentralized manner, ensuring data integrity and security without the possibility of manipulation. The research methods used are literature review, needs survey, design, development, comparison and evaluation. The result achieved was an evoting application based on a website platform by implementing blockchain technology that can ensure data security.

articleTitle: Enhancing Road Repair Management in Indonesia Through Open Participatory Reporting Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: In Indonesia, roads are crucial for regional connectivity and economic growth. Effective road maintenance management is primarily managed by the Ministry of Public Works and Public Housing (PUPR) in collaboration with local governments, focusing on addressing forms of road deterioration such as potholes, cracking, rutting, and raveling. The open participatory model capitalizes on the high usage of mobile phones in Indonesia, projected to reach 97% by 2029, encouraging community participation in infrastructure management by enabling users to report road conditions in real-time using features such as GPS and camera functionality. The implementation of a digital map-based reporting system using OpenStreetMap and an AI-assisted mobile application enhances public involvement, fosters transparency, and improves road safety through real-time monitoring and efficient resource allocation by relevant authorities. This approach empowers citizens and promotes a safer traveling environment, ultimately contributing to better infrastructure management and community ownership.

articleTitle: Analysis of Market Potential and Business Model of Establishment of Automotive Parts Startup in the Digital Era With the Lean Startup Method
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: In the rapidly evolving digital era, there is an increasing need for efficiency and innovation in the supply of automotive parts. The main problems are identifying potential market segments and developing a business model that can compete in this dynamic industry. The methodology applied in this study is a lean start-up approach that involves a build-measure-learning stage. This study aims to analyze the market potential and right business model for the establishment of an automotive part startup in the digital era using the lean startup method. The first stage is the development of an ((MVP) to obtain initial feedback from potential customers. The data obtained from this stage were then analyzed to determine the validity of the initial hypothesis and repeat the product. In addition, a comprehensive market study is conducted to understand consumer needs and preferences and to analyze market trends. The results of this study show significant market potential for automotive parts startups that integrate digital technology into their operations, which contributes to strategic recommendations for the establishment and development of startups in this sector.

articleTitle: Shortcut on the Edge of the Cliff: An Overview of Artificial Intelligence for Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: In recent decades, the influence of technological advancement has reached various domains including education. Accordingly, during these latest years, the development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has become paramount in the domain of education. Responding to that situation, this article undertakes a systematic review to investigate the opportunity and risk of artificial intelligence use in education, especially in tertiary education context. To support the investigation, this study assembled a dataset of 22 published articles from 2019 to 2023 from the reputable research article database. Here, the study focused on the application of artificial intelligence (AI), particularly Chat GPT, in higher education. Based on the analysis, the results showed that Chat GPT use has both positive and negative effects on students and lecturers. The positive effects include the creation of educational content, personalized learning experiences, increased student engagement, and an enhanced learning environment. The negative effects included an increased risk of plagiarism, educational inequality, impact on human skills and interaction, and teacher-student dynamics. These findings provide important information for educational stakeholders and support the assessment and evaluation of AI use in academic activities.

articleTitle: The Technology Development and Application of Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) in the Agriculture Field in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: In the last few decades, agricultural technology, including Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV), has been very rapid. For this reason, there is a need to research the scientific structure related to the development of agricultural technology and UAV applications, especially in Indonesia. The research takes a comprehensive literature study to provide information on the appropriate use of agricultural technology and UAV applications to increase productivity. UAV applications in the agricultural sector in Indonesia include mapping and surveying agricultural land, monitoring plant health and growth, spraying fertilizers and pesticides, estimating crop yields, irrigation management, data analysis, and weather monitoring. The development program for the use of UAVs in the agricultural sector in Indonesia has great potential to continue to develop in the future. However, there are obstacles to the application of UAVs in the agricultural sector, including high costs and low accessibility, limited skills and knowledge of farmers, maintenance and sustainability, infrastructure, diversity, and local needs. In the future, several main areas are likely to become the focus of research and development, including precision mapping, crop monitoring, precision agriculture, big data in agriculture, IoT integration, UAV battery technology, UAV safety system, technology adaptation for local commodities, and UAV training programs for farmers.

articleTitle: Weather Detection System Using Cloud Images Based on Histogram Analysis as An Aviation Safety Effort
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference of Adisutjipto on Aerospace Electrical Engineering and Informatics (ICAAEEI)
abstract: In the autopilot system, the aircraft must know the weather conditions in front of it through a camera to record it as a flight history or decide what steps to take in dealing with these weather conditions. In contrast to sunny and cloudy conditions, overcast conditions have two possibilities. The plane can continue its journey by penetrating the cloudy weather or avoiding it if the cloudy clouds contain lightning with too high a frequency. This study uses histogram analysis to separate the two weather conditions, cloudy and gloomy. It also separates gloomy conditions into overcast and hurricane conditions using the nearest neighbor method of the standard deviation of the data testing and data training. The program is also used to convert Red, Green, and Blue (RGB) images into grayscale and to determine the pixel value of each image test data, which is then displayed as a histogram graphical result. The results showed that the detection system could perform weather detection with the results of image test data, as many as 57 images, 45 data with successful status, and 12 data with failed status. The experiment failed because the number of pixel brightness values between the training and test data did not match the weather being tested. Based on this test, it was found that the proportion of system success was 78.95%.
